parsed.why: Beyond the severe national framework, the state imposes birth-sex facility and prison placement rules, bars trans women from shelters, and criminalises some gender expression. The above-background killing estimate adds concern, though it is based on few cases.

The additional facility restriction is limited to public-school students; no statewide adult facility rule or trans-specific violence pattern is documented. This leaves the serious national document and entry exposures as the main visitor risks.

State rules add school restrictions, a bathroom misdemeanour in specified circumstances, and removal of X markers from state licences. Enforcement is undocumented, but these restrictions compound the national visitor-facing risks.

A state law criminalises birth-sex-incongruent restroom use across public buildings and public-facing private businesses, with possible jail time. This universal, visitor-facing exposure adds materially to the national document regime; litigation is not a demonstrated remedy.

The state adds no statewide adult facility ban or documented visitor-targeting practice; its bathroom restriction is district-specific and applies to students. Limited local protections do not offset the severe national document and entry risks.
